summary: SpatialDDS is an open protocol, published as a draft by the Open AR Cloud association, for sharing live spatial information between robots, vehicles, phones, sensors and digital twins. It builds on the Object Management Group's Data Distribution Service, a publish-and-subscribe messaging standard, and defines typed messages for poses, coordinate frames, anchors, maps, sensor streams, detections, zones and events, with discovery by place and web-readable manifests. It covers positioning, frames, discovery, anchors and sensor data in depth, and it carries large content such as meshes and splats by reference rather than defining those formats. It leaves rendering, avatars, audio, physics, scripting, payments and scene graphs to others, and its own text says its subject is observations and predictions about the physical world. A standards audience should know that version 1.8 is a draft in which any minor release may still break the wire format before formal adoption, and that the Neural, Agent and Open World Model profiles that look closest to metaverse needs are informative or provisional examples outside the normative text.

coverage.note: SpatialDDS carries live state from robots, vehicles, tracked entities and sensors, including detections and sensor streams, to subscribers such as digital twin backends over publish-subscribe.
